claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: The average extent of ligation per junction during synthesis of t5 '+' and '−' strands was 78%.
claims.source: Operating across 70 distinct ligation junctions in these reactions including AU-rich sequences, t5+1demonstrates the sequence generality for self-synthesis using triplet substrates. Notably, the average extent of ligation per junction during synthesis of t5 '+' and '−' strands (78%) was similar to that observed when t5+1 used an unstructured model template (74%, Figure 3c) upon which the parental Z and other RPRs excel (Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claims.claim: t5+1 could assemble synthesised '+' strand segments into αβ+ and γδε+ fragments, guided only by partially overlapping '−' strands.
claims.source: At this point, we tested whether the broad oligonucleotide ligation capacity of t5+1 (Figure 3c) might allow assembly of synthesised '+' strand segments. Indeed, t5+1 could assemble these into αβ+ and γδε+ fragments, guided only by partially overlapping '−' strands (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claims.claim: The ribozyme-synthesised αβ+ and γδε+ fragments spontaneously reconstituted a new catalytically active triplet polymerase ribozyme through non-covalent association.
claims.source: Through non-covalent association (Vaish et al., 2003; Mutschler et al., 2015), the ribozyme-synthesised αβ+ and γδε+ fragments spontaneously reconstituted a new catalytically active triplet polymerase ribozyme (with in vitro transcribed type 1 RNA).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claims.claim: The ribozyme-synthesized and assembled triplet polymerase could regenerate fresh δ- segment using t5+1 ribozyme-synthesised δ+ as a template.
claims.source: We found that this synthesis product could regenerate fresh δ- segment using t5+1 ribozyme-synthesised δ+ (left over from ribozyme assembly) as a template (Figure 6c), recapitulating elements of a self-replication cycle.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: More concentrated triplet substrates can successfully compete with ribozyme unstructured elements for hybridization to '−' strand templates.

claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: t5+1 can extend primers bidirectionally, in both the canonical 5'−3' as well as the reverse 3'−5' directions.
claims.source: Unexpectedly, triplet substrates provide a route to bypass the 'primer problem'. We observed that t5+1 can extend primers bidirectionally, in both the canonical 5'−3' as well as the reverse 3'−5' directions (Figure 7a).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7a.

claims.claim: t5+1 can achieve 'primer free' RNA synthesis.
claims.source: Given this flexibility, we wondered if t5+1 even had a requirement for a primer oligonucleotide. Indeed, this triplet polymerase could achieve 'primer free' RNA synthesis (whereby synthesis is presumably initiated by ligation of adjacent triplets anywhere on the template), as exemplified here for the β+ segment (Figure 7b), as well as 'primer free' RNA replication as shown for the '+' and '−' strands of the γ segment, which can be replicated using triplets alone (Figure 7c).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claims.claim: Random sequence triplet pools ('pppNNN') could be used as substrates by t5+1 in segment syntheses in place of defined triplet sets.

claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: Extension activity remained robust upon pool supplementation with noncanonical dinucleotide and mononucleotide substrates.
claims.source: Furthermore, extension activity remained robust upon pool supplementation with noncanonical dinucleotide and mononucleotide substrates (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5.

claims.claim: The starting Zcore ribozyme exhibited approximately 91% fidelity per position.
claims.source: On average, the starting Zcore ribozyme exhibited ~91% fidelity per position (Figure 8a), lower than that described for RPRs (92% – 97% [Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016]).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8a and citations.

claims.claim: Zcore accuracy exhibited a pronounced downward gradient from the first (5') to the third (3') triplet position.
claims.source: Furthermore, its accuracy exhibited a pronounced downward gradient from the first (5') to the third (3') triplet position, highlighting escalating risks to fidelity of synthesis founded on longer building blocks.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: The final t5+1 ribozyme achieves an average positional fidelity of 97.4% using pppNNN.
claims.source: Notably, the final t5+1 ribozyme achieves an average positional fidelity of 97.4% using pppNNN in this sequence context, higher than the best RPR fidelity with NTPs under comparable eutectic conditions (Attwater et al., 2013b).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citation.

claims.claim: Deep sequencing of internal triplet positions of a defined sequence (β+ segment) synthesised by t5+1 using pppNNN indicated similar aggregate fidelity could be achieved during longer product synthesis excluding the final triplet.
claims.source: Deep sequencing of internal triplet positions of a defined sequence (β+ segment) synthesised by t5+1 using pppNNN indicated similar aggregate fidelity could be achieved during longer product synthesis excluding the final triplet (Table 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Table 1.

claims.claim: The type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute to fidelity gains.
claims.source: Investigating the fidelity contributions of different t5+1 ribozyme components, we found that the type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute; rather, fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain, as its deletion (yielding the truncated 'αβγδ' ribozyme) reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain.
claims.source: Investigating the fidelity contributions of different t5+1 ribozyme components, we found that the type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute; rather, fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain, as its deletion (yielding the truncated 'αβγδ' ribozyme) reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Presence of the ε domain selectively reduced the most acute errors at the second and third triplet positions.
claims.source: Presence of the ε domain did not uniformly increase fidelity, but selectively reduced the most acute errors at the second and third triplet positions (with over 10-fold reductions for some errors, Figure 8b, Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claims.claim: Overall error rates at the second and third triplet positions were reduced by 4-fold and 9-fold compared to Zcore.
claims.source: Overall error rates at the second and third triplet positions were reduced by 4-fold and 9-fold compared to Zcore (Figure 8a), though increased (1.3-fold) at the first triplet position due to a localised asymmetric tolerance of G:U wobble pairing (Figure 8b).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claims.claim: The ε domain fidelity function is contingent upon the presence of a downstream triplet.
claims.source: The ε domain fidelity function is contingent upon the presence of a downstream triplet, operating only with basal fidelity for final triplet incorporation (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Using triplet substrates modified at the third position with a 2-thiouracil in place of a uracil rendered the ε fidelity domain unable to discriminate mismatches.
claims.source: Dissecting the molecular determinants of the fidelity phenotype, we found that using triplet substrates modified at the third position with a 2-thiouracil in place of a uracil (disrupting minor groove hydrogen bonding capabilities) rendered the ε fidelity domain unable to discriminate mismatches (Figure 8c, Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claims.claim: Inclusion of complementary triplets caused a striking (~3 fold) drop in misincorporation errors in some direct pair-mispair triplet contests.
claims.source: We observed that in some direct pair-mispair triplet contests, inclusion of their complementary triplets caused a striking (~3 fold) drop in misincorporation errors (Figure 9).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9.

claims.claim: Raising pppNNN concentrations from 0.5 to 5 μM each almost halved the overall error rate.
claims.source: Indeed, counterintuitively, raising pppNNN concentrations from 0.5 to 5 μM each almost halved the overall error rate (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The fidelity enhancement at higher pppNNN concentrations was driven by pronounced reductions in errors where the mismatched triplet has a high GC content compared to the cognate triplet.
claims.source: Although diverse effects upon individual misincorporations were observed, this fidelity enhancement was driven by pronounced reductions in errors where the mismatched triplet has a high GC content compared to the cognate triplet, including common G-U wobble mispairs (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: More efficient, higher fidelity segment synthesis was observed when using an pppNNN pool formulated with a reduced G content.
claims.source: Indeed, more efficient, higher fidelity segment synthesis was observed when partially mimicking this outcome using an pppNNN pool formulated with a reduced G content (Figure 6—figure supplement 4, Table 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures and table.

claims.claim: The triplet polymerase ribozyme comprises a heterodimer of a catalytic triplet polymerase subunit (t5) and a non-catalytic RNA cofactor (type 1).
claims.source: Here, we describe the discovery and characterization of a ribozyme (t5+1) with a robust ability to polymerize RNA trinucleotide triphosphate (triplet) substrates. Unusually, this triplet polymerase ribozyme comprises a heterodimer of a catalytic triplet polymerase subunit (t5) and a non-catalytic RNA cofactor (type 1), which enhances triplet polymerase activity and abrogates the need for template tethering.
claims.evidence: This is a summary finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: The quaternary structure of the triplet polymerase ribozyme is reminiscent of the processivity factors of some proteinaceous polymerases such as the heterodimeric p66/p51 HIV reverse transcriptase holoenzyme.
claims.source: Such a quaternary structure - involving a heterodimer of a full-length and a truncated subunit - is reminiscent of the processivity factors of some proteinaceous polymerases such as the heterodimeric p66/p51 HIV reverse transcriptase holoenzyme (Huang et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison, supported by citation.

claims.claim: The spontaneous emergence of a general, mutualistic RNA cofactor has not previously been observed for ribozymes.
claims.source: However, the spontaneous emergence of a general, mutualistic RNA cofactor has not previously been observed for ribozymes and may suggest an underappreciated dimension to the evolutionary dynamics of ribozyme pools under stringent adaptive pressures.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding, representing knowledge about the field.

claims.claim: The t5+1 ribozyme's principal current shortcoming is its low catalytic efficiency.
claims.source: The t5+1 ribozyme's principal current shortcoming is its low catalytic efficiency.
claims.evidence: This is an assessment of the ribozyme's performance based on experimental data.

claims.claim: In the optimal context for mononucleotide polymerase ribozymes, the triplet polymerase heterodimer yields approximately 4 fold more unligated junctions than the RPR tC19Z.
claims.source: In the optimal context for mononucleotide polymerase ribozymes, this triplet polymerase heterodimer yields ~4 fold more unligated junctions than the RPR tC19Z (Attwater et al., 2013b), which itself is 240-fold slower than the currently most advanced RPR 24–3 (Horning and Joyce, 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claims.claim: When binding templates, triplets incur a lower entropic cost per position compared to canonical mononucleotides.
claims.source: For instance, when binding templates, triplets incur a lower entropic cost per position compared to canonical mononucleotides (thus aiding copying of sequences rich in weakly pairing A and U bases), with particularly helpful stability contributions from intra-triplet base stacking (Eigen, 1971).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the molecular properties of triplets, supported by citation.

claims.claim: Energetically favourable inter-triplet stacking interactions appear to instigate cooperative binding and unfolding of even highly stable RNA template structures upon reaching the required substrate concentration threshold.
claims.source: Furthermore, energetically favourable inter-triplet stacking interactions appear to instigate cooperative binding and unfolding of even highly stable RNA template structures (Figures 1b and 5a) upon reaching the required substrate concentration threshold.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of cooperative binding, supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claims.claim: A general solution to the copying of structured RNAs arises from conditions that promote base-pairing rather than conditions that disfavour it.
claims.source: Counterintuitively, a general solution to the copying of structured RNAs arises not from conditions that disfavour base-pairing (which would also hinder substrate binding), but rather from conditions that promote it.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the experimental findings about triplet-based RNA synthesis.

claims.claim: A triplet/template duplex presents a more ordered, regular target for sequence-general ribozyme docking than a single stranded template.
claims.source: A triplet/template duplex presents a more ordered, regular target for sequence-general ribozyme docking (by e.g. the ε domain) than a single stranded template (variably prone to secondary structure formation or sequence-specific interactions with the ribozyme [Wochner et al., 2011]).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the structural basis of ribozyme function, supported by citation.

claims.claim: Mechanistic analogies between the triplet polymerase ribozyme and the ribosome are apparent.
claims.source: While phylogenetically unrelated, mechanistic analogies between the triplet polymerase ribozyme and the ribosome are apparent. Both are RNA heterodimers that operate in a triplet register along a single-stranded RNA template, whilst enforcing a minor-groove mediated pattern of triplet or anticodon readout (including tolerance of 5' wobble pairing), suggestive of convergent adaptive solutions to the challenges of replication and decoding.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of structural and functional features.

claims.claim: It has long been speculated that the decoding centre of the small ribosomal subunit might have had its origins in an ancestral RNA replicase.
claims.source: It has long been speculated that the decoding centre of the small ribosomal subunit might have had its origins in an ancestral RNA replicase, but the implied triplet-based character of such a replicase was conspicuously discordant with modern mononucleotide-based replication (Weiss and Cherry, 1993; Poole et al., 1998; Noller, 2012).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about prior speculation in the field, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The utility of triplets as substrates for RNA synthesis and self-synthesis suggests that early ideas about the ribosome's origins in an RNA replicase deserve to be reconsidered.
claims.source: The utility of triplets as substrates for RNA synthesis and self-synthesis described herein suggests that these early ideas deserve to be reconsidered.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the findings of the study.

claims.claim: An early reliance upon triplets in RNA replication could have inadvertently supplied a decoding center for translation.
claims.source: In the context of initial uncorrelated evolution of the small and large ribosomal subunits (Petrov et al., 2015), it is tempting to speculate that an early reliance upon triplets in RNA replication could have inadvertently supplied a decoding center for translation.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the findings of the study and citation.

claims.claim: Short RNA oligonucleotides may represent predisposed substrates for RNA-catalyzed RNA replication.
claims.source: In conclusion, the unexpected emergent properties of triplets – including cooperative binding and unfolding of structured RNA templates, enhanced incorporation of AU-rich substrates, and error attenuation (resulting from triplet pool interaction networks) – argue that short RNA oligonucleotides may represent predisposed substrates for RNA-catalyzed RNA replication.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claims.claim: Some benefits of triplets might extend to codon/anticodon dynamics in early translation.
claims.source: Some of these benefits might also extend to codon/anticodon dynamics in early translation, and to the non-enzymatic replication of RNA (Szostak, 2012), where downstream trinucleotides have recently been shown to enhance incorporation of preceding activated mononucleotides both through stacking and positioning effects (Vogel et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2018) and the formation of a highly reactive intermediate (Prywes et al., 2016; O'Flaherty et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to related work.

claims.claim: The interaction of triplet substrate pools with RNA templates promotes uncoupling of an RNA's sequence from its replicability.
claims.source: Taken together, the interaction of triplet substrate pools with RNA templates promotes uncoupling of an RNA's sequence (i.e. information content, and associated folding tendencies) from its replicability, thereby enhancing RNA's capacity to serve as an informational polymer.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claims.claim: Z RPR has only a very limited template ligation activity slightly exceeding background nonenzymatic ligation.
claims.source: Z RPR has only a very limited template ligation activity (slightly exceeding background nonenzymatic ligation [Rohatgi et al., 1996]).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and citation.

claims.claim: 3' truncation of Z RPR abolished mononucleotide polymerase activity but accommodated and enhanced templated ligation.
claims.source: In contrast, 3' truncation (which abolished mononucleotide polymerase activity) accommodated and enhanced templated ligation.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The selection strategy required iterative templated triplet ligation by ribozymes to achieve their covalent linkage to a tagged primer.
claims.source: We devised a selection strategy that required iterative templated triplet ligation by ribozymes to achieve their covalent linkage to a tagged primer (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental design of the selection strategy.

claims.claim: Transplanting the conserved 5' 'cap+' sequence from types 2–6 allows the Zcore but not the 0core ribozyme triplet polymerase activity to be enhanced by type 1.

claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: RNA polymerase activity of Z RPR using NTPs is enhanced by type 1 addition, but only when modified with the 5' 'cap+' sequence.
claims.source: Right, RNA polymerase activity of Z RPR using NTPs is enhanced by type 1 addition, but only when modified with the 5' 'cap+' sequence (Z RPRcap+), extending primer A10 on tethered template HTI (0.5 μM of each RNA, 4 mM of each NTP, at 4˚C for 68 hr).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The type 0 ribozyme had gone extinct by round 21 of selection.
claims.source: At this point, the type 0 ribozyme had gone extinct, replaced by six new types of RNA each characterised by a unique 3' domain (Figure 2a, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by sequencing data.

claims.claim: Six new types of RNA (types 1-6) emerged by round 21, each characterised by a unique 3' domain.

claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by sequencing data.

claims.claim: Type 5 was the fastest enriching triplet polymerase ribozyme in the final selection pool.
claims.source: In complex with type 5 (the fastest enriching triplet polymerase ribozyme in the final selection pool), type 1 boosts polymerization of triplets (or longer oligonucleotides) to enable synthesis of long RNAs (Figure 3c).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by selection data.

claims.claim: RPRs generally depend upon tethering to template due to their poor affinity for primer/template duplex.
claims.source: Due to their poor affinity for primer/template duplex (Lawrence and Bartel, 2003), RPRs generally depend upon such tethering to template (Attwater et al., 2010; Wochner et al., 2011; Horning and Joyce, 2016), which enhances local ribozyme concentration and promotes formation of the RPR-primer/template holoenzyme (Attwater et al., 2010; Attwater et al., 2013a).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about RPRs supported by citations.

claims.claim: The 8S hairpin template had previously strongly arrested even the most advanced mononucleotide RPRs at higher temperatures.

claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Synthesis by the Z RPR is completely arrested by the 6S and 8S hairpins.
claims.source: While all hairpin templates are robustly copied by t5+1, synthesis by the Z RPR is completely arrested by the 6S and 8S hairpins.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claims.claim: The Broccoli aptamer is a fluorescent RNA aptamer.

claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: The catalytic t5 ribozyme was divided into five segments α, β, γ, δ and ε.
claims.source: As t5+1 currently lacks the efficiency to synthesise RNAs its own length, we divided the catalytic t5 ribozyme into five segments α, β, γ, δ and ε.
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental strategy used in the study.

claims.claim: Segmentation strategy could reduce tertiary structures and ease product separation during RNA replication.
claims.source: This segmentation strategy (akin to that used by some RNA viruses e.g. influenza) could reduce tertiary structures (Doudna et al., 1991; Mutschler et al., 2015) and ease product separation during RNA replication (Szostak, 2012).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of segmentation, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The geometric mean of the final extents of ligation across all 70 junctions in the self-synthesis context was 78%.
claims.source: Densitometry gave yields of full-length products (boxed, by % of total primer), and a geometric mean of the final extents of ligation across all 70 junctions in this self-synthesis context (78%).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: The ribozyme-synthesized and assembled αβ+/γδε+ ribozyme is as active as in vitro transcribed equivalents.
claims.source: The ribozyme-synthesized and assembled αβ+/γδε+ ribozyme is as active as in vitro transcribed equivalents, and can efficiently utilize ribozyme-synthesized RNA (δ+) as a template.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: Efficiency of both segment synthesis and assembly will need to be increased significantly to realise a full self-replication cycle.
claims.source: However, while the t5+1 ribozyme displays a nascent capacity for templated synthesis of its own catalytic domain '+' strands (and '−' strands), efficiency of both segment synthesis and assembly will need to be increased significantly to realise a full self-replication cycle (which would also require synthesis and replication of the type 1 subunit).

claims.source: However, while the t5+1 ribozyme displays a nascent capacity for templated synthesis of its own catalytic domain '+' strands (and '−' strands), efficiency of both segment synthesis and assembly will need to be increased significantly to realise a full self-replication cycle (which would also require synthesis and replication of the type 1 subunit).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about requirements for full self-replication.

claims.claim: Some specific oligonucleotide substrates were required for efficient synthesis of α+ and ε+ segments to compete out inhibitory mutual hybridisation between '−' strand template and corresponding '+' strand unstructured elements in the t5 ribozyme.
claims.source: In particular, some specific oligonucleotide substrates were required for efficient synthesis of α+ and ε+ segments to compete out inhibitory mutual hybridisation between '−' strand template and corresponding '+' strand unstructured elements in the t5 ribozyme (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: In vitro selections that stabilise the ribozyme tertiary structure may contribute to attenuating the requirement for specific oligonucleotide substrates.
claims.source: In vitro selections that stabilise the ribozyme tertiary structure (Figure 6—figure supplement 3) may contribute to attenuating this requirement.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about future improvements, supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: All RPRs require primers to initiate syntheses, akin to the activity of replicative polymerases in biology.
claims.source: The majority of specific oligonucleotides, however, were provided as primers to initiate syntheses, as required by all RPRs akin to the activity of replicative polymerases in biology.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about RPRs and biological polymerases.

claims.claim: The priming sequence would effectively be excluded from evolution during replication.
claims.source: As a consequence of this, the priming sequence would effectively be excluded from evolution during replication.

claims.claim: RNA oligonucleotides able to act as specific primers are unlikely to be prevalent in prebiotic substrate pools.
claims.source: Furthermore, RNA oligonucleotides able to act as specific primers are unlikely to be prevalent in prebiotic substrate pools, and their depletion during successive replication cycles could lead to loss of sequence at genome ends.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about prebiotic chemistry.

claims.claim: The 'primer problem' has previously been noted in the context of nonenzymatic replication as one of the fundamental obstacles to RNA self-replication.
claims.source: This 'primer problem' has previously been noted in the context of nonenzymatic replication (Szostak, 2012) as one of the fundamental obstacles to RNA self-replication.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Bidirectional extension allows not only completion of RNA synthesis from either template end but also initiation from anywhere along a template.
claims.source: This allows not only completion of RNA synthesis from either template end but also initiation from anywhere along a template, potentially allowing non-classical hierarchical or distributive RNA replication schemes as previously proposed (Szostak, 2011).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the implications of bidirectional extension, supported by citation.

claims.claim: Primer-free RNA synthesis is presumably initiated by ligation of adjacent triplets anywhere on the template.
claims.source: Indeed, this triplet polymerase could achieve 'primer free' RNA synthesis (whereby synthesis is presumably initiated by ligation of adjacent triplets anywhere on the template), as exemplified here for the β+ segment (Figure 7b), as well as 'primer free' RNA replication as shown for the '+' and '−' strands of the γ segment, which can be replicated using triplets alone (Figure 7c).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of primer-free synthesis.

claims.claim: A ribozyme operating in a more distributive polymerisation mode might be able to replicate RNA sequences directly from pools of short random RNA oligonucleotides furnished by prebiotic chemistry.
claims.source: Such a ribozyme operating in a more distributive polymerisation mode might be able to replicate RNA sequences directly from the putative pools of short random RNA oligonucleotides furnished by prebiotic chemistry.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about potential prebiotic applications.

claims.claim: A replicase must incorporate the correct template-complementary substrate from random sequence pools, or genetic information may become irretrievably corrupted during replication.
claims.source: However, a replicase must incorporate the correct template-complementary substrate from random sequence pools, or genetic information may become irretrievably corrupted during replication (Eigen, 1971).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: The fidelity challenge is exacerbated in triplet-based RNA replication by the need to discriminate between 64 distinct substrates.
claims.source: The fidelity challenge is exacerbated in triplet-based RNA replication by the need to discriminate between 64 distinct substrates; indeed, a previous investigation into the incorporation of individual trinucleotides indicated that misincorporations could outstrip cognate incorporation for some triplets (Doudna et al., 1993).

claims.source: The fidelity challenge is exacerbated in triplet-based RNA replication by the need to discriminate between 64 distinct substrates; indeed, a previous investigation into the incorporation of individual trinucleotides indicated that misincorporations could outstrip cognate incorporation for some triplets (Doudna et al., 1993).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Zcore fidelity is lower than that described for RPRs (92% – 97%).
claims.source: On average, the starting Zcore ribozyme exhibited ~91% fidelity per position (Figure 8a), lower than that described for RPRs (92% – 97% [Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016]).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claims.claim: t5+1 fidelity is higher than the best RPR fidelity with NTPs under comparable eutectic conditions.
claims.source: Notably, the final t5+1 ribozyme achieves an average positional fidelity of 97.4% using pppNNN in this sequence context, higher than the best RPR fidelity with NTPs under comparable eutectic conditions (Attwater et al., 2013b).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citation.

claims.claim: Deletion of the ε domain reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore.
claims.source: Investigating the fidelity contributions of different t5+1 ribozyme components, we found that the type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute; rather, fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain, as its deletion (yielding the truncated 'αβγδ' ribozyme) reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Error rates at the first triplet position increased 1.3-fold due to a localised asymmetric tolerance of G:U wobble pairing.
claims.source: Overall error rates at the second and third triplet positions were reduced by 4-fold and 9-fold compared to Zcore (Figure 8a), though increased (1.3-fold) at the first triplet position due to a localised asymmetric tolerance of G:U wobble pairing (Figure 8b).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claims.claim: A similar replacement of a uracil 2-keto group with a 2-thio modification had been shown to impair Z RPR activity when present upstream in the primer/template region.
claims.source: Previously, a similar replacement of a uracil 2-keto group with a 2-thio modification had been shown to impair Z RPR activity when present upstream in the primer/template region (Attwater et al., 2013a), where Z is thought to rely upon sequence-general minor groove contacts through an 'A-minor' motif (Shechner et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Z is thought to rely upon sequence-general minor groove contacts through an 'A-minor' motif.
claims.source: Previously, a similar replacement of a uracil 2-keto group with a 2-thio modification had been shown to impair Z RPR activity when present upstream in the primer/template region (Attwater et al., 2013a), where Z is thought to rely upon sequence-general minor groove contacts through an 'A-minor' motif (Shechner et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Modification at the third triplet position reverts ε's divergent effects on fidelity at the adjacent second and the distal first triplet positions.
claims.source: Modification at the third triplet position reverts ε's divergent effects on fidelity at the adjacent second and the distal first triplet positions (Figure 8—figure supplement 3); disruption of this minor groove contact site thus abolishes overall ε fidelity domain operation.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: ε sensitivity to minor groove composition may be critical to its recognition of cognate Watson-Crick base pairs.
claims.source: ε sensitivity to minor groove composition may be critical to its recognition of cognate Watson-Crick base pairs, reminiscent of Tetrahymena group I intron folding (Battle and Doudna, 2002) and the decoding centre of the ribosome (which also tolerates wobble pairing at the analogous (5') triplet position) (Ogle et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of fidelity, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The decoding centre of the ribosome tolerates wobble pairing at the analogous (5') triplet position.
claims.source: ε sensitivity to minor groove composition may be critical to its recognition of cognate Watson-Crick base pairs, reminiscent of Tetrahymena group I intron folding (Battle and Doudna, 2002) and the decoding centre of the ribosome (which also tolerates wobble pairing at the analogous (5') triplet position) (Ogle et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Differential formation of triplet:anti-triplet dimers in the reaction may explain the drop in misincorporation errors upon inclusion of complementary triplets.
claims.source: A potential explanation may arise from differential formation of triplet:anti-triplet dimers in the reaction: for example, more extensive pppGCC:pppGGC (than pppACC:pppGGU) dimer formation would selectively reduce the effective concentration of free pppGCC vs. pppACC upon inclusion of their complementary pppGGC and pppGGU.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of fidelity enhancement.

claims.claim: Dimer formation among pppNNN substrate pools would be expected to selectively buffer the free concentrations of the more strongly-pairing GC-rich triplets.
claims.source: Dimer formation among pppNNN substrate pools would be expected to selectively buffer the free concentrations of the more strongly-pairing GC-rich triplets, which could promote both fidelity and sequence generality through normalization of triplet availability against template (and complementary triplet) binding strength.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of fidelity enhancement.

claims.claim: The potential for replication to proceed in different triplet registers may provide a degree of resilience towards biases in substrate pool composition.
claims.source: However, the potential for replication to proceed in different triplet registers may provide a degree of resilience towards such biases.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the robustness of triplet-based replication.

claims.claim: There are multiple examples of dimerization in RNA evolution.
claims.source: There are multiple examples of dimerization in RNA evolution - such as the VS ribozyme (Suslov et al., 2015), retroviral RNA genome dimerization (Paillart et al., 2004), in vitro evolved heterodimeric RNA liposome binders (Vlassov et al., 2001), and recently the homodimeric CORN fluorescent RNA aptamer (Warner et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The extinction of previously dominant species in the selection that were unable to benefit from type 1 enhancement illustrates the potential for symbioses to shape RNA molecular ecologies.
claims.source: Indeed, the extinction of previously dominant species in the selection that were unable to benefit from type 1 enhancement (e.g. type 0, see Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and succession with cooperative RNA species (Vaidya et al., 2012) illustrates the potential for such symbioses to shape RNA molecular ecologies.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary dynamics, supported by data and citation.

claims.claim: Despite modest catalytic power, t5+1 displays much enhanced generality in RNA synthesis.
claims.source: Yet despite this modest catalytic power, t5+1 displays much enhanced generality in RNA synthesis and now achieves both copying of previously intractable structured RNA templates, and templated synthesis and assembly of an active '+' strand copy of its catalytic domain, suggesting key contributions of the triplet substrates themselves.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of findings from the study.

claims.claim: The process of cooperative binding and unfolding is aided by the cold temperature and solute concentration effects of eutectic ice phase formation.
claims.source: In our work, this process is aided by the cold temperature and solute concentration effects of eutectic ice phase formation (Attwater et al., 2010; Mutschler et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by citations.

claims.claim: General duplex interactions underlie other notable features observed in triplet-based RNA synthesis such as in trans template binding.
claims.source: Such general duplex interactions also underlie other notable features observed in our triplet-based RNA synthesis such as in trans template binding (Figure 3c) as well as the capacity for bidirectional (5'−3'/3'−5') and primer-free RNA synthesis (Figure 7).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the structural basis of observed features, supported by data.

claims.claim: RNA-catalyzed triplet polymerisation can proceed with a fidelity matching or exceeding even the best mononucleotide RNA polymerase ribozymes.
claims.source: Contrary to expectations RNA-catalyzed triplet polymerisation can proceed with a fidelity matching or exceeding even the best mononucleotide RNA polymerase ribozymes (Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claims.claim: t5+1 ribozyme fidelity is due to both a readout of cognate minor groove interactions by the ribozyme ε domain and an unanticipated fidelity boost arising from systems-level properties of triplet pools.
claims.source: t5+1 ribozyme fidelity is due to both a readout of cognate minor groove interactions by the ribozyme ε domain (Figure 8) and an unanticipated fidelity boost arising from systems-level properties of triplet pools, that appear to normalize the availability of free triplet (and potentially longer oligonucleotide) substrates against their base-pairing strength (Figure 9).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of findings from the study supported by data shown in figures.

claims.claim: Triplet pool properties likely involve formation of cognate or near-cognate triplet:anti-triplet interaction networks.
claims.source: Though further work will be required to characterize triplet pool properties, they likely involve formation of cognate or near-cognate triplet:anti-triplet interaction networks, as formation of tRNA dimers via cognate anticodon:anticodon interactions has been observed in a similar concentration range (Eisinger and Gross, 1975).
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism, supported by citation to analogous observations.

claims.claim: Both the triplet polymerase ribozyme and the ribosome are RNA heterodimers that operate in a triplet register along a single-stranded RNA template.
claims.source: Both are RNA heterodimers that operate in a triplet register along a single-stranded RNA template, whilst enforcing a minor-groove mediated pattern of triplet or anticodon readout (including tolerance of 5' wobble pairing), suggestive of convergent adaptive solutions to the challenges of replication and decoding.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of structural and functional features.

claims.claim: The implied triplet-based character of an ancestral RNA replicase was conspicuously discordant with modern mononucleotide-based replication.
claims.source: It has long been speculated that the decoding centre of the small ribosomal subunit might have had its origins in an ancestral RNA replicase, but the implied triplet-based character of such a replicase was conspicuously discordant with modern mononucleotide-based replication (Weiss and Cherry, 1993; Poole et al., 1998; Noller, 2012).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about prior speculation in the field, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Initial evolution of the small and large ribosomal subunits was uncorrelated.
claims.source: In the context of initial uncorrelated evolution of the small and large ribosomal subunits (Petrov et al., 2015), it is tempting to speculate that an early reliance upon triplets in RNA replication could have inadvertently supplied a decoding center for translation.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Downstream trinucleotides have recently been shown to enhance incorporation of preceding activated mononucleotides both through stacking and positioning effects.
claims.source: Some of these benefits might also extend to codon/anticodon dynamics in early translation, and to the non-enzymatic replication of RNA (Szostak, 2012), where downstream trinucleotides have recently been shown to enhance incorporation of preceding activated mononucleotides both through stacking and positioning effects (Vogel et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2018) and the formation of a highly reactive intermediate (Prywes et al., 2016; O'Flaherty et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to recent work.

claims.claim: Downstream trinucleotides enhance incorporation of preceding activated mononucleotides through the formation of a highly reactive intermediate.
claims.source: Some of these benefits might also extend to codon/anticodon dynamics in early translation, and to the non-enzymatic replication of RNA (Szostak, 2012), where downstream trinucleotides have recently been shown to enhance incorporation of preceding activated mononucleotides both through stacking and positioning effects (Vogel et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2018) and the formation of a highly reactive intermediate (Prywes et al., 2016; O'Flaherty et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to recent work.

results.result: In vitro evolution of a truncated Z RPR (Zcore) yielded an improved triplet polymerase ribozyme (type 0/0core) after 7 rounds of selection. This ribozyme could catalyze iterative triplet polymerization and copy structured templates that were intractable to the parental Z RPR, with primer extension showing sigmoidal dependence on triplet concentration suggestive of cooperative structure invasion.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C26 and C84-C86 describe the initial evolution and characterization of the 0core ribozyme with consistent experimental evidence from Figures 1a-c and supplementary figures. The sigmoidal concentration dependence (C25) is directly shown in Figure 1c, and the ability to copy structured templates (C24) is demonstrated in Figure 1b. The selection strategy (C86) is detailed in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

results.result: After 21 rounds of selection, six new RNA types (1-6) emerged, with type 1 comprising ~50% of sequences but being catalytically inactive. Type 2-6 RNAs displayed triplet polymerase activity that was substantially enhanced by equimolar addition of type 1 RNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C30 and C89-C90 are well-supported by sequencing data (Figure 2a, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and activity assays (Figure 2b). The emergence of a catalytically inactive but mutualistic RNA species (type 1) is a novel finding with clear experimental demonstration of activity enhancement across multiple ribozyme types.

results.result: Type 1 RNA functions as a non-catalytic cofactor that forms a 1:1 heterodimeric complex with active triplet polymerases through interaction at the 'cap+' hairpin. The 5' truncation of type 1 did not affect cofactor activity, and transplanting the 'cap+' sequence to other ribozymes conferred type 1 responsiveness.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C33 and C87-C88 are supported by gel mobility shift assays (Figure 3b), activity enhancement experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and domain swapping experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 2). The 1:1 stoichiometry is demonstrated both by gel shift and by the ~50% abundance of type 1 in the selection pool.

results.result: The type 5 + type 1 heterodimer (t5+1) enables synthesis of long RNAs using triplet or oligonucleotide substrates and obviates the need for ribozyme-template tethering through true intermolecular, sequence-general interaction with primer-template duplexes.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C36 and C68 are supported by experimental data in Figure 3c showing long RNA synthesis with both cis and trans template configurations. The ability to function without tethering represents a significant advance over previous RPRs and is clearly demonstrated.

results.result: The final t5+1 triplet polymerase ribozyme comprises a 135 nt type 1 subunit and a 153 nt t5 catalytic subunit, emerging from in vitro evolution as a mutualistic RNA heterodimer.
results.evaluation: Claims C37 and C4 are supported by structural data in Figure 4 and the evolutionary trajectory documented through the selection. The heterodimeric architecture is well-characterized through multiple experiments.

results.result: The t5+1 ribozyme robustly copied hairpin-containing templates with estimated TMs up to 93°C (8S template), which had previously arrested even advanced mononucleotide RPRs. Triplet concentration-dependent cooperative structure invasion was recapitulated with the 8S template, while dinucleotide substrates only extended up to the structured region.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C40, C5, and C94 are strongly supported by experimental data in Figure 5a and supplementary figures. The comparison with Z RPR shows complete arrest at 6S and 8S hairpins, while t5+1 achieves robust copying. The cooperative mechanism is demonstrated through concentration-dependence studies (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).

results.result: The t5+1 ribozyme synthesized both a functional fluorescent '+' strand of the 52 nt Broccoli RNA aptamer and its encoding '−' strand template from their constitutive triplets.
results.evaluation: Claim C41 is supported by experimental data in Figure 5b showing both SYBR Gold staining and DFHBI-1T fluorescence, confirming functional aptamer synthesis. This demonstrates sequence generality and the ability to synthesize both strands of a functional RNA.

results.result: The t5+1 ribozyme achieved synthesis of multiple segments (β+, γ+, δ+ and all '−' strands α-, β-, γ-, δ-, ε-) from constitutive triplets starting from ~8 nt primers, though α+ and ε+ required some pre-linked oligonucleotides. The average ligation efficiency across 70 junctions was 78%.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C45, C8, C96, and C98 are supported by experimental data in Figure 6a and Figure 6—figure supplement 1. The requirement for longer oligonucleotides for α+ and ε+ is explained by competition with ribozyme-template pairing (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). The 78% average ligation efficiency is comparable to performance on unstructured templates.

results.result: The t5+1 ribozyme assembled synthesized '+' strand segments into αβ+ and γδε+ fragments, which spontaneously reconstituted a catalytically active triplet polymerase ribozyme through non-covalent association. This ribozyme-synthesized and assembled enzyme could regenerate fresh δ- segment using ribozyme-synthesized δ+ as template.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C48, C9, and C99 are supported by experimental data in Figure 6b-c and Figure 6—figure supplement 1. The activity of the assembled ribozyme matches in vitro transcribed controls (Figure 6c), demonstrating successful self-synthesis and assembly. This represents a key step toward self-replication.

results.result: While t5+1 displays nascent capacity for self-synthesis, efficiency of both segment synthesis and assembly needs significant improvement to realize full self-replication, which would also require synthesis and replication of the type 1 subunit. Some specific oligonucleotides were required for α+ and ε+ synthesis due to inhibitory template-ribozyme hybridization.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C103 represent honest assessment of current limitations supported by experimental data (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). The requirement for longer oligonucleotides in some syntheses and the need for type 1 replication are acknowledged limitations that prevent claiming full self-replication.

results.result: The t5+1 ribozyme can extend primers bidirectionally in both canonical 5'→3' and reverse 3'→5' directions, supporting non-canonical bidirectional modes of RNA synthesis and replication.
results.evaluation: Claims C50, C6, and C7 are supported by experimental data in Figure 7a showing extension of fluorescein-labeled primers from both template ends. This bidirectional capability is a unique feature enabled by triplet substrates.

results.result: The t5+1 ribozyme can achieve 'primer-free' RNA synthesis, presumably initiated by ligation of adjacent triplets anywhere on the template, as demonstrated for the β+ segment and for replication of the γ segment '+' and '−' strands using triplets alone.
results.evaluation: Claims C51 and C109 are supported by experimental data in Figure 7b-c showing synthesis without added primers. The 10% yield for γ+ and 6% for γ- (Figure 7c) demonstrates proof-of-principle, though efficiency is lower than primer-dependent synthesis. The mechanism (ligation of adjacent triplets) is inferred but reasonable.

results.result: Random sequence triplet pools (pppNNN) comprising all 64 triplets could be used as substrates by t5+1 in segment syntheses, and extension activity remained robust upon pool supplementation with dinucleotide and mononucleotide substrates.
results.evaluation: Claims C52 and C53 are supported by experimental data in Figure 6—figure supplement 4 and Figure 6—figure supplement 5. The ability to use random pools is critical for potential prebiotic relevance and demonstrates sequence generality.

results.result: The starting Zcore ribozyme exhibited ~91% fidelity per position with a pronounced downward gradient from first to third triplet position. The final t5+1 ribozyme achieves 97.4% average positional fidelity using pppNNN, higher than the best RPR fidelity with NTPs under comparable conditions. Similar aggregate fidelity was achieved during longer β+ segment synthesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C57, C114, and C115 are supported by deep sequencing data (Figure 8a, Table 1). The fidelity measurements are rigorous, using 12 different template sequences and analyzing thousands of sequences. The comparison to RPRs is appropriately cited. The gradient in Zcore fidelity highlights the challenge of longer building blocks.

results.result: Fidelity gains in t5+1 are mediated by the newly-evolved ε 3'-domain rather than the type 1 cofactor. The ε domain selectively reduced errors at second and third triplet positions (4-fold and 9-fold reductions) but increased errors at the first position (1.3-fold) due to tolerance of G:U wobble pairing.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C61 and C116 are supported by deletion analysis (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) and detailed error profiling (Figure 8a-b, Figure 8—figure supplement 2). The position-specific effects are well-documented, showing selective rather than uniform fidelity improvement.

results.result: The ε domain fidelity function requires a downstream triplet and depends on minor groove interactions. Modification at the third triplet position with 2-thiouracil rendered the ε domain unable to discriminate mismatches and abolished overall fidelity domain operation.
results.evaluation: Claims C62, C63, and C120 are supported by experiments with modified triplets (Figure 8c, Figure 8—figure supplement 3). The 2-thiouracil modification experiments provide strong evidence for minor groove-mediated fidelity discrimination. The requirement for a downstream triplet is clearly demonstrated.

results.result: Inclusion of complementary triplets caused ~3-fold drops in misincorporation errors in some pair-mispair contests. Raising pppNNN concentrations from 0.5 to 5 μM almost halved the overall error rate, driven by reductions in errors where the mismatched triplet has high GC content. Higher fidelity segment synthesis was observed with reduced-G pppNNN pools.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C67 are supported by experimental data in Figure 9 and supplementary figures. The concentration-dependent fidelity enhancement is counterintuitive but well-documented. The GC-content dependence suggests triplet pool interaction networks buffer availability of strongly-pairing triplets. The low-G pool experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 4, Table 1) provide additional support.

results.result: Differential formation of triplet:anti-triplet dimers may explain fidelity enhancement upon inclusion of complementary triplets. Dimer formation among pppNNN pools would selectively buffer free concentrations of GC-rich triplets, normalizing availability against base-pairing strength. Triplet pool properties likely involve cognate or near-cognate interaction networks.
results.evaluation: Claims C123, C124, and C133 represent mechanistic speculation about triplet pool behavior. While the fidelity data (C64-C67) are solid, the proposed dimer formation mechanism lacks direct experimental evidence. The analogy to tRNA dimer formation (cited) is suggestive but not definitive. Further characterization of triplet pools is explicitly acknowledged as needed.

results.result: The t5+1 ribozyme's principal shortcoming is low catalytic efficiency, yielding ~4-fold more unligated junctions than RPR tC19Z in optimal contexts. Despite this modest catalytic power, t5+1 displays enhanced generality in RNA synthesis, achieving copying of structured templates and self-synthesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C71, C72, and C128 provide honest assessment of ribozyme performance. The efficiency comparison to tC19Z and 24-3 RPRs (with appropriate citations) contextualizes the limitations. The trade-off between efficiency and generality is well-documented through the experimental results.

results.result: Triplets incur lower entropic cost per position than mononucleotides when binding templates, with favorable intra- and inter-triplet stacking interactions. These interactions instigate cooperative binding and unfolding of stable RNA structures. The solution to copying structured RNAs arises from conditions promoting base-pairing rather than disfavoring it. Triplet/template duplexes present more ordered targets for ribozyme docking than single-stranded templates.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C76, C129, and C130 represent mechanistic interpretations supported by experimental observations (sigmoidal concentration dependence, structure invasion) and theoretical considerations (cited). The cooperative binding model explains the observed data. The role of eutectic ice phase is supported by citations and experimental conditions.

results.result: Mechanistic analogies exist between the triplet polymerase ribozyme and the ribosome: both are RNA heterodimers operating in triplet register along single-stranded RNA templates, enforcing minor-groove mediated readout patterns including tolerance of 5' wobble pairing. The ribosome's decoding center also tolerates wobble pairing at the analogous position.
results.evaluation: Claims C77, C121, C122, and C134 draw well-supported analogies between t5+1 and the ribosome. The structural and functional parallels (heterodimer, triplet register, minor groove readout, wobble tolerance) are documented. The ribosome comparison is appropriately cited (Ogle et al., 2001). These represent convergent solutions to similar problems.

results.result: It has been speculated that the ribosome's decoding center might have originated from an ancestral RNA replicase, but the implied triplet-based character was discordant with modern mononucleotide-based replication. The utility of triplets demonstrated here suggests these ideas deserve reconsideration. An early reliance on triplets in RNA replication could have inadvertently supplied a decoding center for translation.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80, C135, and C136 represent evolutionary speculation. While C78, C135, and C136 accurately cite prior speculation, C79 and C80 are new speculations based on the current findings. The connection between triplet-based replication and ribosome origins is intriguing but remains speculative without additional evidence. This is appropriately presented as speculation ('tempting to speculate').

results.result: The emergent properties of triplets (cooperative binding/unfolding, enhanced AU-rich incorporation, error attenuation) argue that short RNA oligonucleotides may represent predisposed substrates for RNA-catalyzed replication. Benefits might extend to codon/anticodon dynamics and non-enzymatic replication. Triplet pool interactions promote uncoupling of RNA sequence from replicability.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C83 represent conclusions drawn from the experimental findings. C81 and C83 are well-supported by the demonstrated properties of triplet-based synthesis. C82 is more speculative but appropriately cites relevant work on non-enzymatic replication. The conclusion about uncoupling sequence from replicability is a key insight supported by the structure invasion data.

results.result: The quaternary structure of t5+1 (heterodimer of full-length and truncated subunit) is reminiscent of processivity factors like HIV reverse transcriptase. The spontaneous emergence of a general mutualistic RNA cofactor has not been previously observed for ribozymes. The extinction of type 0 and succession with cooperative species illustrates potential for symbioses to shape RNA molecular ecologies.
results.evaluation: Claims C69, C70, C126, and C127 discuss the novelty and evolutionary implications of the heterodimeric architecture. The comparison to HIV RT (C69) is appropriately cited. The novelty claim (C70) is supported by knowledge of the field. The evolutionary dynamics (C127) are documented through the selection data showing type 0 extinction and type 1 emergence.

results.result: RNA-catalyzed RNA replication is believed to have supported primordial biology, but RNA catalysis depends on folding that yields structures blocking replication. This creates an antagonism between RNA's ability to fold for function and ease of replication. Even highly-evolved RPRs are substantially impeded by template secondary structures that are ubiquitous and indispensable in functional RNAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C10, C11, C16-C18 establish the background and motivation for the study. These represent established knowledge in the field, appropriately cited (Crick 1968, Orgel 1968, Szostak et al. 2001, Boza et al. 2014, Horning and Joyce 2016). The 'structure vs. replication paradox' is well-documented.

results.result: Prior work on RNA self-replication includes self-splicing intron derivatives and ligase ribozymes that assemble strands from segments (requiring ≥8 nt building blocks), and RNA polymerase ribozymes using NTPs. RPRs depend on template tethering due to poor primer/template affinity and require primers like biological polymerases. Models of non-enzymatic polymerization yield pools dominated by short oligonucleotides. Previous work indicated misincorporations could outstrip cognate incorporation for some triplets.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C15, C19, C92, C104, C107, C111, and C113 summarize relevant prior work, all appropriately cited. These establish the context for the current study and identify limitations of previous approaches (segment length requirements, template structure sensitivity, primer requirements, fidelity challenges).

results.result: More concentrated triplet substrates can compete with ribozyme elements for template hybridization. The priming sequence would be excluded from evolution during replication, and specific primers are unlikely in prebiotic pools. Bidirectional extension allows initiation from anywhere along a template, potentially enabling non-classical replication schemes. A distributive ribozyme might replicate sequences from random oligonucleotide pools.
results.evaluation: Claims C49, C102, C103, C105, C106, C108, and C110 discuss implications and potential solutions to the primer problem. C49 and C102 are supported by experimental data (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). C105-C106 and C110 represent reasonable inferences about prebiotic scenarios. C108 appropriately cites Szostak 2011 for non-classical replication schemes.

results.result: The fidelity challenge is exacerbated in triplet-based replication by needing to discriminate between 64 substrates. However, the potential for replication in different triplet registers may provide resilience toward biases in substrate pool composition.
results.evaluation: Claims C112 and C125 discuss fidelity challenges and potential solutions. C112 is supported by citation to prior work (Doudna et al. 1993). C125 represents speculation about robustness but is reasonable given the demonstrated flexibility of the system.

results.result: The Broccoli aptamer is a fluorescent RNA aptamer. Segmentation strategy could reduce tertiary structures and ease product separation, akin to influenza virus strategy. Prior work showed 2-thio modification impairs Z RPR activity in primer/template regions where Z relies on A-minor motif contacts. Downstream trinucleotides enhance mononucleotide incorporation through stacking/positioning and reactive intermediate formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C95, C97, C118, C119, C137, and C138 provide supporting context and cite relevant prior work. All citations are appropriate and support the stated claims. These provide background for experimental design choices and mechanistic interpretations.
